Many people say the 1648 Peace of Westphalia invented the modern state. Historians argue over that. The war behind it is not in doubt: it killed millions.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The Thirty Years' War ran from 1618 to 1648, mostly in Central Europe. Estimates of the dead run from 4.5 to 8 million soldiers and civilians, from battle, famine and disease.

2/ It began with a Prague Castle quarrel in May 1618: Protestant nobles threw two of Ferdinand's Catholic representatives and their secretary out of a window. All three survived. The war that followed did not.

3/ Look at the two maps. In 1618 the Holy Roman Empire is one big block. By 1650 it's a patchwork, and the big powers around it look much the same. The Empire's changes were constitutional, not just territorial.
4/ The Empire had about 300 imperial estates. Westphalia confirmed their autonomy and the supremacy of the Imperial Diet, and it ended the rule that subjects must follow their ruler's religion.

5/ Some of the map changed hard: Sweden gained Western Pomerania, France gained Alsatian cities, Brandenburg-Prussia gained Farther Pomerania, and the Swiss Confederacy gained legal independence from the Empire.

6/ 'Westphalian sovereignty' is the idea that 1648 created a system of independent states. Some scholars call it a later story built in the 19th and 20th centuries. The treaties mattered, but maybe not for that reason.
7/ Did 1648 invent the modern state system, or did we write that history afterwards? Read the full story in our newsletter: https://buttondown.com/forummapping
